title: The MDX portability scan misses image alt text and autolink angle brackets
description:
Filed from the LCLI-663 review (opum-control review.recorded seq 7977, run job-0ac7fxs). Both gaps were examined during that review and reported as NOT introduced by LCLI-663 -- they are pre-existing in mdxHazardFindings and were out of scope for that task.

THE TWO GAPS. (1) Image alt text is never scanned: `![alt {x}](u)` produces an mdast `image` node carrying alt as a STRING property with no text child, so mdxHazardFindings sees neither the `{` nor any entity inside it. (2) An autolink's angle brackets go unmatched: `<https://x/>` exposes only the inner URL as text, so the `<`/`>` that MDX would parse are never seen.

WHY IT MATTERS. Both are MDX hazards (or near-hazards) the check's own premise says it should catch -- a raw `{` in image alt text breaks a Docusaurus build exactly as it does in prose. The reviewer probed both; neither was caught.

SUGGESTED FIX: scan `image` alt (the inline image node's `alt` string, and any HTML alt form) for un-escaped, non-code `<`/`{`; and decide DELIBERATELY whether an autolink's angle brackets are a hazard, recording the decision either way -- "not flagged" should be a ruling, not an oversight.

NOT STAMPED: no assignee; opum-doc decides whether it is dispatched.
